_exec_summary.SummaryText:
This program is intended by the City of Tulare Wastewater Treatment Plant (Tulare WWTP) to meet the spirit and intent of the following regulations:
- California Accidental Release Prevention (CalARP) Program - Title 19 CCR, Division 5, Chapter 2
- U.S. EPA Risk Management Program (RMP) - Title 40 CFR §68

Hereafter, this program will be referred to as the CalARP/RMP program.

This program is intended to be a living document. As such, the information, procedures, policies, and documentation that make up this program must be made easily accessible and updated as necessary. To accomplish this, Tulare WWTP has elected to use PSMWriter, software developed and distributed by Resource Compliance, Inc. This software will assist us with updating, maintaining, scheduling, and tracking CalARP/RMP-related activities.

1.1 Tulare WWTP, CalARP/RMP Program

This is to inform all interested persons, including employees, that Tulare WWTP has developed its unified CalARP/RMP Program. This program has been prepared to address the risks involved in operating and maintaining the following process, which has the presence of hazardous chemicals above threshold quantities:

Process Name                       | Process Chemical                         | Process Quantity (lbs.)
Storage and Treatment        Aqueous Ammonia                        120,000

Our CalARP/RMP program promotes overall plant, worker, and public safety. The program enables our facility to prevent the occurrence and minimize the consequences of significant releases of hazardous chemicals. Overall, the program is designed to prevent accidental fatalities, injuries, illnesses, and physical property damage.

Our company has many policies and procedures in place to promote overall plant, worker, and public safety. We have:
1. Prepared a CalARP/RMP program based on the CalARP/RMP regulations
2. Organized the program so that it meshes closely with general business practices
3. Utilized PSMWriter software to ensure that all

necessary employees have access to relevant information (SOPs, PHAs, audits, etc.)

The CalARP/RMP program sets forth rules, procedures, and practices that will help our employees and neighbors protect themselves. 

1.2 Process Descriptions

Facility Overview

The Tulare WWTP operates a wastewater treatment facility for domestic and industrial sewer users in Tulare, CA. The facility has an aqueous ammonia storage and treatment system that provides aqueous ammonia to the Bulk Volume Fermenter (BVF) treatment process.

Facility Location

The Tulare WWTP is located at 1875 S. West Street, Tulare, CA 93274. The latitude and longitude of the storage vessel are 36.187505, -119.374957. The facility is located approximately 2.6 miles west of State Highway 99 in a rural area surrounded primarily by agricultural land.

According to FEMA Flood Map Service, the facility is located in an area of minimal flood hazard.
Tulare WWTP is not located in an Alquist-Priolo Fault Zone as defined by the California Department of Conservation. In addition, a review of United States Geological Survey (USGS) fault maps revealed that there are no faults in close proximity to the site. The USGS 2018 One-Year Model revealed that Tulare WWTP had a 1-2% chance of experiencing potentially minor damage due to ground shaking in 2018.

The USGS 2023 50-State Long-term National Seismic Hazard Model revealed that Tulare WWTP has a 50-75% chance of slight (or greater) damaging earthquake shaking in 100 years.

Description of Covered Process

The aqueous ammonia process at Tulare WWTP involves the storage and proportional dosing of 30% aqueous ammonia for wastewater pH adjustment. No chemical reactions take place during the storage process, and the aqueous ammonia is neutralized after dosing into the Bulk Volume Fermenter (BVF) feed.

Process Classification

The aqueous ammonia storage and treatment process (AA Process) at Tulare WWTP consists of a vessel, equipment, and valves that are interconnecte

d by piping. As such, the aqueous ammonia treatment system at Tulare WWTP is treated as a single process.

1.3 General Accident Release & Chemical Specific Prevention Steps

1.3.1 General 

We inform our employees engaged in process operations of the dangers of an accidental release of a covered chemical in annual safety meetings. These employees are made aware of the potential risks of the process chemicals involved. During these meetings, we also discuss preventative measures, such as evacuation, in order to be prepared for a release. 

Tulare WWTP has also conducted an off-site consequence analysis of worst-case and alternate-case release scenarios for the process. These are for the purposes of informing the public in the event of an accidental release. The results of the analyses are reported in the body of the program. 

1.3.2 Aqueous Ammonia

The storage and treatment process at the Tulare WWTP facility is an integral part of the overall business and operates most of the year. The process includes an aqueous ammonia storage vessel with a maximum inventory of 120,000 lbs of 30% aqueous ammonia. It is extremely important that this process is maintained and operated in a safe and efficient manner. Management is committed to making sure that employees are made aware of the potential danger of an ammonia leak.

Our operations and maintenance personnel monitor the process and keep an active log of all procedures and transactions that pertain to aqueous ammonia. In addition, the process is checked frequently by one of the outside sensor contractors that we use. 

1.4 Five-Year Accident History

Tulare WWTP has had no accidental release within the last five years.

1.5 Emergency Action and Response Plan 	

Tulare WWTPs emergency action and response program has been developed to satisfy the following requirements:
Cal/OSHAs Emergency Action Plan  Title 8 CCR §3220
U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administrations (OSHA) Emergency Action Plans  Title 29 CFR §1910

.38
California Accidental Release Prevention (CalARP/RMP) Program [Emergency Response Program Requirements]  Title 19 CCR, Division 5, Chapter 2 §5120.1-5120.2
California Hazardous Materials Business Plan (HMBP) [Emergency Response Plans and Procedures]  Title 19 CCR, Division 5, Chapter 1 §5030.7

Strategically, we will respond minimally to a release. Under this plan we will call emergency personnel and evacuate the facility. All response activities would be done in coordination with the Local Fire Department and their Hazardous Materials Response Team. 

Every year, we review with our employees our evacuation procedures in the event of an emergency, including a hazardous chemical release.

1.6 Planned Changes to Improve Safety

Tulare WWTP has implemented many policies and procedures to promote overall plant, worker and public safety. Nevertheless, Tulare WWTP continually strives to improve in all areas, including safety.

By utilizing PSMWriter software, all necessary employees have access to every aspect of the CalARP/RMP program. This has improved Tulare WWTPs ability to communicate hazardous situations to employees and contractors. In addition, PSMWriter tracks all CalARP/RMP-related events so that Tulare WWTPs management team can ensure that the CalARP/RMP program is being implemented.

Tulare WWTP has implemented all aspects of the CalARP/RMP program. When a CalARP/RMP program requirement is completed (i.e. mechanical integrity inspection, hazard review, compliance audit, etc.), then any specific action items related to that event are entered into PSMWriter, assigned a responsible person, and given a due date. Once the action item has been completed, the resolution can be documented using PSMWriter. A list of current or past due action items can be accessed at any time by those with access to PSMWriter.

In addition to utilizing PSMWriter to create, schedule, track, and document events, Tulare WWTP has also entered into a contract with Resource Complia

nce to obtain help with CalARP/RMP program implementation.

For the future, Tulare WWTP now thinks of the CalARP/RMP program as a living document. It is an interactive framework that guides safe action for Tulare WWTP employees, but allows for feedback and continual improvement. Through the CalARP/RMP program, Tulare WWTP will continue to maintain overall plant worker and public safety.
